key_insight: Simplifying thermal assumptions in laser-arc hybrid welding simulation can cut runtime dramatically while preserving most predictions, with morphology-mapped heat input offering the best efficiency-fidelity balance.
engineering_relevance: For thermo-elastic-plastic welding analysis, the study shows where expensive physics can be removed without losing key outputs like distortion and residual stress trends.
method: Compared three FE thermo-elastic-plastic models on the same SBHS400 butt joint mesh
Model 1 used a combined cylindrical–double-ellipsoid heat source with latent heat and radiation
Model 3 replaced the analytical source with a GUI-mapped equivalent volumetric heat flux from the fusion-zone macrograph
evidence_signal: The models were checked against thermocouple histories, out-of-plane distortion, and XRD residual stress measurements, with runtime dropping from 57.3 h to 20.5 h and then 17.5 h.
watch_item: The morphology-mapped uniform heat flux can smear stresses, so local peak stresses near the weld toe/fusion zone may be less reliable than with higher-fidelity thermal physics.
paper_title: Effect of thermal modeling assumptions on prediction accuracy and computational efficiency in laser-arc hybrid welding simulation
